# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)

# Full breakdown in tooltips of end of turn dialog

## Problem statement

The end-of-turn ledger tooltips (added by MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO) attach to every
row, but most of them summarise rather than explain: breakdowns are rendered as a
single comma-joined `Per item: A: +5, B: +7` line, the total rows only say "The
sum of the lines above", the supplementary context rows restate their own label,
and no tooltip shows the item's **base value ± each named modifier**. The player
cannot see how a row's total was actually calculated — for example, which part of
a staff member's salary is base and which part is the Operations Manager
discount.

## Users

- **The human player** — reads the Turn Summary after each closing and needs to
  understand exactly how each figure arose, so the next day's decisions are
  informed.
- **Competitive players** — need the same detail on their own seat's tab.

### User stories

- _As a player, I want the Staff wages tooltip to list each staff member on its
  own line with the Base Cost and each +/- modifier (e.g. Operations Manager),
  so I can understand each member's true salary._
- _As a player, I want the income tooltips to list each contributing business on
  its own line, and the Event income tooltip to name each event effect and its
  coins, so I can see what drove my income._
- _As a player, I want the Total rows to list the lines that make them up, so I
  can reconcile the subtotal myself._
- _As a player, I want the Incident and supplementary rows to show the numbers
  behind them, not just a sentence repeating the row label._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Staff wages** tooltip lists each staff member on its own line, showing the
   base salary and every named modifier with its signed amount (e.g.
   `Operations Manager: -50`), computing the member's charged salary, then
   reconciling the list to the committed category total (including the existing
   street-wide reduction and available-coins clamp lines).
2. **Community spaces** and **Business costs** tooltips list each space/business
   on its own line with its base ongoing cost (not a comma-joined single line),
   still reconciling to the committed category total via the street-wide Cost
   Cutter reduction and clamp lines.
3. **All four income rows** (Base, Synergy, Reputation, Events) list each
   contributing business on its own line; the **Event income** tooltip
   enumerates each event effect (`name: signed delta`) rather than only a
   per-business sum.
4. **Incident** tooltip names the resolved incident and shows each modifier
   applied to its effect (e.g. Brand Ambassador reputation multiplier) so the
   committed coin/reputation deltas are reproducible; the "no incident" note is
   unchanged.
5. **Total income** and **Total operating expenses** tooltips enumerate each
   contributing line with its amount and reconcile to the committed subtotal,
   replacing "The sum of the lines above".
6. **Supplementary context rows** show numeric derivations where the projection
   already carries them: closing coins (day start + net change), reputation
   change (income + incident + one-off reputation) and businesses owned (the
   business names, not just a count). Score change keeps its explanatory text
   because challenge-level detail is not carried by the projection.
7. All new copy is localisable through the existing `t()` / `registerLocale`
   system with English defaults registered at module load; tooltips remain
   **presentational** (no state mutation, no RNG), **absent-safe** (a
   legacy/hand-built ledger with no breakdown degrades to the committed total
   plus the existing explanatory note), and render the same detail level for
   single-player and each competitive seat's tab.
8. Deterministic automated tests cover the enhanced content for every row type
   above (staff modifiers, per-business income lines, event-effect enumeration,
   incident modifiers, total-line enumeration, context derivations), added to
   the existing tooltip suites and run through the test skill.
9. Documentation is updated: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (the
   "End-of-Turn Turn Summary Ledger and Tooltips" per-item detail table and
   tooltip-format description) and the JSDoc in
   `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` / `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`.
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Hovering any line in the end-of-turn statement now explains the number behind it
— every staff member's base salary and discounts, every business's contribution,
every event effect, and how the totals add up.

## Constraints

- **Tooltips stay presentational.** No new state mutations and no RNG
  consumption; every figure comes from the committed ledger or the engine's own
  per-item data (`IncomeResult`, `SlotPhaseBreakdown`, `state.staffCards`,
  `state.streetGrid`).
- **Do not invent attribution.** Where the ledger carries no per-item data the
  tooltip must fall back to the committed total with an explanatory note, never
  a synthesised split.
- **One-off per-source attribution is out of scope.** `TurnLedger.oneOffDeltas`
  is a residual aggregate; a true per-source breakdown needs engine-level
  attribution in `buildTurnLedger` and is recorded as a follow-up work item.
  The one-off tooltip keeps its documented reconciliation formula.
- **Existing interaction and styling unchanged.** `attachHudTooltipZone` hover/
  tap behaviour, lazy content building, and the `TooltipManager` styling are not
  touched; only content builders and the data threaded into them change.
- **No layout regression.** Multi-line tooltips must fit the existing tooltip
  width/wrapping behaviour; no dialog re-layout.
- **Single-player and competitive parity.** Income detail exists for both;
  competitive expense rows are category-total only today (`OwnerRoundLedger`
  carries no per-card detail) and stay that way unless per-seat detail is
  derived — see A2.

## Existing state

- **Tooltip builders**: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` (334
  lines) — `buildIncomeLineTooltip`, `buildExpenseLineTooltip`,
  `buildTotalLineTooltip`, `buildIncidentLineTooltip`,
  `buildOneOffLineTooltip`, `buildNetLineTooltip`, `buildContextLineTooltip`,
  plus the `LEDGER_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `LEDGER_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English bundle.
- **Projection model**: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` —
  `PLProjection` / `PLStatementLine` / `PLBreakdownItem` (`{ name, coins }`) /
  `PLLineBreakdown` (`{ items, streetReduction? }`), `incomeLineBreakdown`
  (line 1029) and `expenseLineBreakdown` (line 1070).
- **Data already available**:
  - staff: `state.staffCards[]` with `ongoingCost` and skills;
    `computeStaffSalaryCost` / `computeStaffSalaryDiscount` /
    `getSalaryScopeSkills` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:852-877`), skill name
    `Operations Manager` (`src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts:99`);
  - community / business: `slot.ongoingCost`, `state.streetGrid`,
    `state.soldSlots`;
  - income: `SlotIncome` (`baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `total`) and
    `SlotPhaseBreakdown` (`baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `repBonus`,
    `eventDeltas[]`);
  - incident: `TurnResult.incident` (`EventCard`, carries its base effect) plus
    `incidentCoinChange` / `incidentRepChange`;
  - context: `closingBalances` (day start + net) and `businessesOwned`.
- **Current shallow behaviour** (confirmed by inspection):
  - expenses render comma-joined: `t('...perItem', { breakdown: 'A: -5, B: -7' })`;
  - totals render `label: amount` + "The sum of the lines above.";
  - context rows render a title + one generic sentence, no numbers;
  - the Event income row derives a per-business sum, discarding each
    `SlotEventDelta.name` / `delta`.
- **Tests**: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` (612 lines, unit
  coverage of every builder) and
  `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltip-attachment.test.ts` (attachment), plus
  browser suites `turn-summary-tooltip.browser.test.ts` /
  `turn-summary-pl-overlay.browser.test.ts`.
- **Docs**: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` § "End-of-Turn Turn Summary
  Ledger and Tooltips" documents the current per-item detail and the one-off
  fallback explicitly.

## Desired change

1. Extend `PLBreakdownItem` with an optional base/adder description so a
   breakdown item can carry `base` plus named `modifiers` while `coins` stays
   the committed contribution. Populate it for staff (`base` = card
   `ongoingCost`, modifier = Operations Manager discount) and leave it absent
   for community/business, where only the base applies.
2. Render expense breakdowns multi-line — one item per line, then the
   reconciling reduction/clamp/total lines.
3. Thread `SlotPhaseBreakdown` detail (including `eventDeltas`) through
   `incomeLineBreakdown` and render income breakdowns multi-line, with the Event
   income row listing each event effect.
4. Add incident modifier detail (reputation-multiplier effects applied to the
   resolved incident) to `buildIncidentLineTooltip`, keeping the `null` fallback.
5. Replace `buildTotalLineTooltip`'s generic note with an enumeration of the
   section's contributing lines and their amounts.
6. Add numeric derivations to the context tooltips that the projection already
   supports (closing coins, reputation change, businesses owned names); leave
   score change as prose.
7. Add the new i18n keys to `LEDGER_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `LEDGER_TOOLTIP_STRINGS`
   and update the docs table.
8. Add/extend deterministic tests for each enhanced builder and for the threaded
   model data.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — multi-line breakdown rendering,
  incident modifier detail, total-line enumeration, context derivations, new
  i18n keys. Replaces the comma-joining `formatBreakdown`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend `PLBreakdownItem` (base +
  modifiers), thread `eventDeltas` / `repBonus` through `incomeLineBreakdown`,
  supply staff base/modifier detail in `expenseLineBreakdown`, extend
  `PLSupplementaryContext` for day-start coins and business names.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — pass the section's lines to
  `buildTotalLineTooltip` and the extra context data; no interaction change
  expected beyond the call sites.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — per-row-type content
  assertions (staff base ± modifier, per-business income lines, event effects,
  incident modifiers, total enumeration, context derivations).
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-pl-model.test.ts` — model-level assertions for
  the new breakdown/modifier fields and absent-safe degradation.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — per-item detail table and tooltip
  format description.

## Related work

- `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` — *Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger* (parent: attached
  the tooltips this item deepens).
- `MS-0MW7QQ5QU007XXC0` — *Attach tooltips to the Turn Summary ledger rows*.
- `MS-0MW7QQ1FD000RCA3` — *Verification: ledger tooltip model and content*.
- `MS-0MW7QQ65P006N3KA` — *Competitive per-seat tooltip parity*.
- `MS-0MW7QQ5BX002KGS0` — *Extend P&L model with per-item breakdowns and tooltip
  content* (the projection/breakdown plumbing this item deepens).
- `MS-0MWBZ05LB007UXQ9` — *Build Summary-row tooltip content builders* (blocked:
  the Summary tab's per-figure tooltips will reuse the per-line builders this
  item improves, so its breakdowns inherit the new detail automatically).
- `MS-0MW6H9A47001B1QT` — *Cards should represent the actual income and
  reputation changes* (same principle of showing the engine's real per-item
  figures rather than card-face values).
- `MS-0MW4MSNWR00123OZ` — *two-type staff skills* (Operations Manager salary
  discount and its business-staff gating).
- `MS-0MW2XMA0Z007MZ6D` — *Draft two-type staff model in GDD*.

## Assumptions & decisions (producer may override)

- **A1 — "Break down the line" means one contributing item per line, with base
  ± named modifiers where the data exists.** For staff that is the base salary
  and the Operations Manager discount; for community/business it is the base
  ongoing cost (the only per-item modifier is street-wide, already a separate
  line). **Recommended** choice, matching the producer's Staff wages example.
- **A2 — Competitive expense rows remain category-total only.** Income detail is
  already per-seat; deriving per-card expense detail for each competitive seat
  would need owner-filtered street/staff derivation and is deferred (recorded as
  a follow-up). Detail level for income/incident/totals/context is identical on
  every tab.
- **A3 — One-off keeps the reconciliation formula.** A per-source split requires
  engine attribution in `buildTurnLedger`; recorded as a follow-up work item
  rather than expanded into this one.
- **A4 — Score change keeps prose.** The projection carries the net score delta
  but not the challenge-level detail needed to show its constituents; extending
  the ledger for that is out of scope.
- **A5 — No layout change.** Multi-line content is assumed to fit the existing
  tooltip width/wrap; if it does not, wrapping is the implementer's call (no
  dialog re-layout).

**Risks**

- *Divergence risk*: re-deriving per-item figures in the UI instead of reading
  the committed ledger could drift from the engine. Mitigation: derive only from
  the engine's own helpers (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, `SlotPhaseBreakdown`) and
  keep the reconcile-to-committed-total lines so any drift is visible in the
  tooltip itself.
- *Regression risk to prior tooltip work*: the parent suite asserts current copy.
  Mitigation: update the assertions deliberately alongside the copy change, and
  keep every existing behaviour (hover/tap, lazy build, absent-safe fallback).
- *Scope-creep risk*: the producer's "each one" could pull in one-off attribution
  and competitive per-card expenses. Mitigation: explicit A2/A3 decisions above,
  with the deferred work linked as follow-up items rather than absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which rows are in scope — every tooltip, or only expenses?** — Answer
  (agent, from seed context + inspection): the seed requests a full breakdown of
  each line ("Staff wages should list each staff member, one per line, with the
  Base Cost +/- any adjustments"). Scope covers income lines, expense lines,
  incident, totals, and the derivable context rows; one-off and score change are
  excluded (A3/A4). Source: seed description; repo inspection of
  `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`.
- **Q: Should a breakdown be one item per line, or is the existing
  comma-separated list acceptable?** — Answer (agent): one item per line, with
  base ± named modifiers, matching the producer's example. **Recommended:**
  one item per line — the comma-joined format is what the producer described as
  "simply repeat the line". Source: seed description.
- **Q: How should the one-off row be broken down?** — **OPEN QUESTION for the
  producer.** `TurnLedger.oneOffDeltas` stores only a residual
  (`netCoinChange - incomeCoins - ongoingTotal - incidentCoinChange`); there is no
  per-source data (market purchases/sales, event plays, Community Favour) to
  attribute. **Recommended:** keep the reconciliation formula here and create a
  follow-up item for engine-level attribution — this keeps the current item
  shippable and avoids inventing splits. Source: `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
  (`oneOffDeltas`) and the existing documented fallback in
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`.
- **Q: Does competitive mode need per-card expense breakdowns?** — Answer
  (agent): income detail is already per-seat; `OwnerRoundLedger` carries no
  per-card expense detail, so deriving it would be new work. **Recommended:**
  defer to a follow-up (A2) and keep income/incident/totals/context at parity on
  every tab. Source: `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` (`buildExpenseRows`).
- **Q: Are single-player and competitive both affected?** — Answer: yes; the same
  builders render every tab, so both benefit wherever the data exists. Source:
  `MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` statement body.

**Headline:** The business Manage Card stops laying off whichever staff member happened to be hired last: it now lists every member employed at that business, one row each with its own `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]`, and an explicit confirm step quoting the exact coins and reputation before anything is charged.

## Problem statement

The Manage Card dialog is the only door for letting business staff go, but it never asks *who*: both `[ Move staff ]` and `[ Lay off ]` act on `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:926,944`). A business holding two or more members therefore exposes one control per action that silently targets the newest hire, and the lay-off executes with no cost preview and no confirmation.

## Users

- **Main Street player with a staffed business (hands-on)** — employs several specialists and wants to change the team.
  - As a player, I want to see everyone employed at this business in one place, with their effect and salary, so that I can decide which specialist is worth keeping.
  - As a player, I want to press a button that belongs to the member I mean, so that I never fire the wrong specialist by accident.
  - As a player, I want the exact coins and reputation the lay-off will charge shown before I commit, so that a €500/turn executive cannot end my run unannounced.
- **Main Street player chasing business efficiency (economy-focused)** — compares each member's salary against its local effect.
  - As a player, I want each row's salary next to the member's effect, so that I can judge the cut by its savings.
- **Game designer / QA** — needs both lay-off doors to state one rule the same way.
  - As QA, I want the quoted cost to equal the charge that lands, so that a skill discount or a clamp cannot silently diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Manage Card dialog renders an **employed-staff section** with exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear. Each row shows the member's name, its role/benefit summary (from a shared formatter, not a UI-invented string) and its effective per-turn salary resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.
- Rows are ordered deterministically (hire order, oldest first) and the panel sizes itself from the row count: at the maximum employment capacity of a business (`level + 1`) every row, button and the sell/close/cancel row are fully visible with no clipping or overlap; with no member employed the section renders nothing at all (today's empty-state behaviour).
- Each row carries `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]` addressed to **that** member. `[ Move ]` hands the member's id to `beginStaffMove`, keeping the existing `moving-staff` choreography, the 1-action cost and the per-member destination list from `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, member.id)` in its hover tooltip. `[ Lay off ]` opens the confirm step for that member only. Because the per-row labels are short, the section states both costs once in its own line (`Move: 1 action · Lay off: 1 turn's salary + reputation`) so neither cost is hidden behind a tooltip. No control in the dialog acts on "the most recently hired" member implicitly.
- The confirm step is an overlay quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (clamped at 0) and the reputation cost from the shared `layOffReputationCost(salary)` — the single formula decided in MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA and **not re-derived here**. `[ Confirm ]` executes `letGoStaffCommand` through the undo manager (the lay-off stays undoable); `[ Cancel ]` changes nothing and returns to the member list.
- After a confirmed lay-off the dialog stays open and re-renders in place: the row disappears, the panel shrinks to fit, and once the last member leaves the staff section disappears while sell/close/cancel keep working. Rows are addressed by **member id** and resolved against `state.staffCards` at click time, so a stale row (the member is already gone, e.g. after an undo) re-renders and flashes feedback instead of acting on a shifted index.
- The activity-log entry and confirmation flash quote the charges actually applied — e.g. `Laid off <name> (−<coins> coins, −<reputation> reputation)` — replacing the hard-coded "−1 salary, −1 reputation" strings.
- Unit tests cover the pure model: membership filtering for the slot, ordering, per-row salary, coin clamp, reputation quote per row, id-addressing/staleness and the empty case; a test pins the confirm step's quoted cost to the effect of `letGoStaffMember()` (quoted == charged) including a discounted-salary member.
- Browser/render tests cover: no affordance when nobody is employed; two employed members produce two rows with two `[ Move ]` and two `[ Lay off ]` controls; the *first* row's `[ Lay off ]` lays off the *first* member (the regression this item exists for) and the *first* row's `[ Move ]` targets the first member; confirm/cancel behaviour; in-place refresh after a lay-off; the section disappearing when the last member leaves; and sell/close/cancel still working.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` D.4.2 §5, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `src/README.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who has hired several specialists at one business can finally pick which one leaves — seeing each member's effect, salary and the exact lay-off price first — instead of a single button that always fires the newest hire.

## Constraints

- **Blocked by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA.** That item lands the salary-scaled reputation rule in `letGoStaffMember()` and exports `layOffReputationCost(salary)`. This item consumes that helper and the same lay-off confirm standard; the formula is not re-litigated here.
- **One confirm step, two doors.** The confirm step is being built for the roster by its child **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ**. This item reuses the shared confirm content builder and cost helpers rather than writing a second quoting implementation; if that child lands the confirm local to the roster dialog, this item factors the shared content builder out and both call it.
- **No engine change.** No new command and no new persisted state. Membership is derived from `state.staffCards` on open and after each action; lay-off stays `letGoStaffCommand` (snapshot → undoable) and relocation stays `moveStaffCommand` (1 action).
- **Address by id, never by index.** `letGoStaffCommand(state, index)` is index-based, so a click resolves the row's member id to a current index at click time and refuses when the member is gone.
- **Pure model first.** Row building, salary/cost resolution and confirm copy live in a Phaser-free module so they are unit-testable; the overlay only draws.
- **One source of truth for figures.** Salaries come from `computeStaffSalaryCost`/`getSalaryScopeSkills`; the lay-off reputation cost from `layOffReputationCost`; the move destinations and 1-action cost from `buildMoveStaffAffordance`. No UI- or model-local arithmetic.
- **Overlay kit only.** `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` / `dismissOverlay`, every element parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, everything tracked in `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), suppressed in `replayMode`/headless runs. No new art — rows are text plus kit buttons.
- **Don't touch the mechanics.** Sell, close, cancel and the move/destination flow keep their current behaviour and costs; only the staff section and its confirm step change.
- **Localisation.** New user-visible strings follow the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English-bundle pattern where a key fits; overlay-only labels may follow the journal/undo-warning literal-string precedent.
- **UK English**, no `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The Manage Card dialog (`showSellConfirmation`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:690-975`) is a fixed 480×410 panel: card info, sale value, a close-cost line, `[ Sell ]` / `[ Close ]` / `[ Cancel ]` at `panelY + 265`, then a single `Employed here: <names>` line (`+305`) and one `[ Move staff (1 action) ]` (`+352, centerX − 110`) plus one `[ Lay off ]` (`+352, centerX + 110`).
- Both staff handlers target the newest hire: `const moveTarget = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`:926`) and `const target = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`:944`). Neither asks for confirmation.
- Membership today: `allStaff.map((member, index) => ({ member, index })).filter(({ member }) => member.employedAtSlot === slotIndex)` (`:700-704`) — the `index` is the `state.staffCards` index `letGoStaffCommand` needs.
- `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) removes the member, charges one turn's effective salary clamped at 0 and a flat **1** reputation, then deregisters it from the business's `employedStaff`. `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps it in a snapshot.
- `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:613`) already accepts an explicit member id, resolves legal destinations through `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` and rejects illegal starts; today the dialog always passes the newest hire. `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:362`) accepts any employed member's id.
- Overlay precedents: `showStorylineJournalDialog()` (`:1655`) row list with empty state and replay short-circuit; `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog()` (`:1227`) is the confirm/cancel shape; `MainStreetLoanSelectorModel` + `MainStreetLoanOverlay` is the pure-model-plus-row-list pair; `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog()` (`:994`) the cost-quote-then-confirm structure.
- `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:452`) already renders per-member `• <name> (<types>) — <description>` lines for the street tooltip — the shared role/benefit text the rows should reuse rather than re-invent.
- The Manage Card only opens for an owned, non-sold, managing-phase slot (`onSellCard` → `showSellConfirmation`), and its handlers carry defensive legality guards; nothing here changes that gating.
- Tests asserting the current behaviour: `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` (lay-off with one member, expects −1 reputation and dialog dismissal; no-affordance empty case), plus `letGoStaffMember`-based expectations in `MainStreetApplicant.test.ts`, `staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` and `MainStreetIntegration.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Pure model** (new `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts`, or a builder added to the roster module MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA creates): `buildBusinessStaffRows(state, slotIndex)` → ordered rows `{ memberId, name, roleSummary, salary, layOffCoins, layOffReputation, moveEnabled, moveDestinations }`, plus `businessStaffIsEmpty(state, slotIndex)`; reuses `layOffReputationCost`, `computeStaffSalaryCost`, `getSalaryScopeSkills`, `buildMoveStaffAffordance` and a shared `formatStaffRoleLine(member)` factored out of `formatEmployedStaffSummary`.
2. **Confirm content builder** (pure): `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` → title/body lines for name, coins and reputation, so the copy and arithmetic are shared with the Company Roster's confirm step rather than duplicated.
3. **Staff rows in the Manage Card** (`showSellConfirmation`): replace the single `Employed here` line and the two fixed buttons with a cost line plus a row list (name · role/benefit · salary, `[ Move ]`, `[ Lay off ]` per row), panel height computed from the row count, and an in-place re-render after a lay-off or a stale-row refusal.
4. **Confirm step**: pressing a row's `[ Lay off ]` shows the confirm overlay (confirm → `letGoStaffCommand` via the undo manager → re-render; cancel → back to the rows untouched).

## Plan: feature decomposition (6 children)

Decision: **full planning** — the `plan-if-needed` pre-check returned `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium; the skip threshold requires risk Low). The plan-approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (approval is required only for **Extra Large** effort **AND** High/Severe risk), so no approval pause was taken.

### Features (in dependency order)

| # | Feature | Item | Depends on |
|---|---------|------|-----------|
| 1 | Test: business-staff row model spec (red first) | MS-0MWCB2YH60070QEW | MS-0MWC9P58U005ZZ18 (engine: `layOffReputationCost()`) |
| 2 | Model: business-staff rows and confirm copy (pure, Phaser-free) | MS-0MWCB2Z20006R9FA | #1, MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM (shared role formatter) |
| 3 | Manage Card: staff rows and per-row `[ Move ]` | MS-0MWCB35QG0030XU6 | #2 |
| 4 | Manage Card: per-row `[ Lay off ]` and confirm step | MS-0MWCB36A8002NKBX | #3, MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ (roster confirm step) |
| 5 | Docs: GDD, catalogue, UX spec and README | MS-0MWCB36TS002IT9J | #3, #4, MS-0MWC9PEPN005SGJ9 (roster docs — same lines) |
| 6 | Verification: full suite and end-to-end flow | MS-0MWCB37G5004ZZ8K | #1–#5 |

### Parent AC → child coverage map

1. Employed-staff section: one row per member at that slot, management-company staff never appear, name/role/salary from the shared helpers → **#2** (model) + **#3** (rows).
2. Hire-order ordering, panel sized from row count, no clipping/overlap at capacity, empty section when nobody is employed → **#2** (ordering) + **#3** (layout).
3. Per-row `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]` addressed to that member, `[ Move ]` → `beginStaffMove` with the `buildMoveStaffAffordance` destinations, no implicit "most recently hired" control, both costs stated in the section's own line → **#2** (ids/move affordance) + **#3** (move UI) + **#4** (lay-off UI).
4. Confirm step quoting name / coins (clamped at 0) / `layOffReputationCost(salary)`, `[ Confirm ]` via `letGoStaffCommand` (undoable), `[ Cancel ]` no-op → **#4**.
5. In-place re-render after a lay-off, panel shrinks, section disappears at the last member, id-addressing with stale-row refusal → **#3** (rebuild helper) + **#4** (behaviour).
6. Log/flash quote the applied charges, replacing the hard-coded strings → **#4**.
7. Unit tests: membership, ordering, per-row salary, clamp, reputation quote, id-addressing/staleness, empty case, quoted == charged → **#1**.
8. Browser/render tests: empty section, two rows/two controls, first-row targeting (the regression), confirm/cancel, in-place refresh, section disappearing, sell/close/cancel intact → **#3**, **#4**.
9. All related documentation updated → **#5**.
10. Full project test suite passes → **#6** (run through the test skill, per the test-execution policy).

The automated `apply_coverage_review(MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11, target_stage="plan_complete")` returned **`proceed`** (100 % coverage, 0 gaps, 0 conflicts) and advanced the stage — no coverage-gap children were created.

### Vertical-slice phasing

Each feature is a minimal end-to-end slice, not a horizontal layer: #1 = failing spec + fixtures; #2 = pure model + shared role line + shared confirm builder + green spec tests; #3 = rows in the dialog, per-row `[ Move ]`, row-count panel height + render tests; #4 = per-row `[ Lay off ]`, confirm overlay, in-place rebuild, stale-row refusal, applied-charge copy + render/undo tests; #5 = docs; #6 = closing verification. Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated if the shipped slice changed an assumption (notably #4 re-reads the Company Roster's shipped confirm implementation before pointing it at the shared builder).

### Test-first ordering

The unit-test specification (#1) is the first child and blocks the model (#2), so the pure contract — including the **quoted == charged** pin against `letGoStaffMember()` — is written and failing before any model code lands. Browser/render tests land with the two UI slices (#3, #4), and #6 is a pure verification checkpoint.

### Scope decisions

- **Single module, shared primitives.** `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` owns the slot rows and the confirm content; it imports `layOffReputationCost()` and the shared role line from the roster/formatting modules the roster child (**MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM**) creates. If the roster module's row shape fits, the builders move there instead (stated in #2) — no second cost or copy implementation either way.
- **Max capacity is 3 today.** `getEmploymentCapacity()` = `max(1, level + 1)` and the largest shipped business `maxLevel` is 2 (`src/card-data.csv`: 4 cards at level 2, 21 at 1, 6 at 0), so the panel-overlap test is asserted at **3 rows** — this resolves one of the effort report's unknowns ("the largest employment capacity reachable in play").
- **Position of last member.** The AC's "once the last member leaves the staff section disappears" is implemented by rebuilding the section from `buildBusinessStaffRows()` — an empty list means no section, exactly today's empty-state behaviour.
- **Documentation sequencing.** #5 depends on the roster's own docs child (**MS-0MWC9PEPN005SGJ9**) because both edit `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` D.4.2 §5 and `docs/game/card-catalog.md`; landing ours second extends that rewrite instead of conflicting with it.
- **No engine change, no new persisted state, no new art** — lay-off stays `letGoStaffCommand`, relocation stays `moveStaffCommand` (1 action), rows are derived from `state.staffCards` on open and after each action.

### Automated review stages

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — every parent AC traced to at least one child (map above); no invented requirements; no contradictory ACs.
2. **Completeness** — all six children carry a `## Acceptance Criteria` section (5–6 ACs) plus Goal, Context, Minimal implementation, Key Files, Dependencies and Deliverables; `validate_key_files_format()` has no complaints (every listed path has a directory segment and an extension; the new module and both test files are covered).
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — spec test → model → rows/move → lay-off/confirm → docs → verification; external edges only to the items that actually supply something (`layOffReputationCost`, the shared role formatter, the roster confirm step, the roster docs).
4. **Scope sizing** — each child is a deliverable increment (≈2–6 h each), none is a horizontal layer.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — every AC is pass/fail-verifiable and names its verification (unit test, render test, doc read, suite run).
6. **Polish & handoff** — each description is copy-pasteable: goal, grounded line references, ACs, minimal implementation, key files, dependencies, deliverables.

### Duplicate-work check

`wl search "business staff lay off member select"` and `wl search "lay off"`: nothing existing covers this scope. Related but distinct: **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (Company Roster overlay — the management-company door, and this item's declared blocker), **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ** / **MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM** (its confirm and model children, supplying the shared confirm builder and role formatter), **MS-0MWC9PEPN005SGJ9** (roster docs, same files), **MS-0MUOSULQ700186PP** (completed; supplied `buildMoveStaffAffordance` / `[ Move staff ]`). No duplicate items were closed or rewritten.

### Appendix (planning session)

No new clarifying questions were asked: the intake Appendix (Q1–Q3, recorded in the item description) already fixes the three design choices this plan depends on — one row per member with its own controls (Q1 = A), per-row `[ Move ]` **and** `[ Lay off ]` (Q2 = B, after research showed `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId)` already takes an explicit member id), and a separate confirm overlay rather than an in-panel state (Q3 = A). No answers were revised.

Decisions taken from existing evidence rather than by asking:

- **Confirm-copy sharing** — the Constraints section already directs it: reuse the roster's shared confirm content builder, and "if that child lands the confirm local to the roster dialog, this item factors the shared content builder out and both call it". Encoded as child #2 (owns `buildLayOffConfirmContent`) and child #4 (points the roster confirm at it). Evidence: item Constraints; MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ AC1.
- **`[ Move ]` availability** — unchanged from today: the control stays visible and `buildMoveStaffAffordance().enabled` drives feedback (tooltip line + illegal-move flash), never row visibility, so a player can always see the whole team. Evidence: `onMoveStaffClick()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:362`) already handles a disabled affordance with feedback.
- **Capacity bound** — 3 members (see Scope decisions).

**OPEN QUESTION** (non-blocking, for the producer): with the salary-scaled reputation rule a lay-off can take reputation to 0 and end the run (€500/turn → 500 reputation; Hard starts at 200). The parent AC only requires the exact figures to be quoted, so this plan ships *quote-only* — no "this ends your run" warning and no refusal. If a warning line or a cap is wanted, it is recorded here as a follow-up rather than folded into these children.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-11 — planned `MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11` (effort Small / risk Medium, no approval pause): created 6 children in test-first dependency order, wired 10 dependency edges (including the 4 external edges to the roster chain), verified AC coverage = 100 % via `apply_coverage_review` (`proceed`), stage advanced to `plan_complete`.
